newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 25.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- EUROTUNNEL URGED TO SEEK RAIL FREIGHT

Deputy UK prime minister John Prescott has told Eurotunnel he will only extend its operating concession contract if it agrees to allow passage of more long-haul rail freight. Holding talks with the French joint chairman of Eurotunnel, Patrick Ponsolle, Prescott expressed a goal of reducing the freight on Europe's roads, a goal tunnel officials stated they would do 'all in their power' to achieve. Eurotunnel insists an extension of its contract is essential to gain the backing of shareholders for an 8.5 billion sterling restructuring plan.
-- ITC FACES CHALLENGE OVER AWARD OF DIGITAL LICENSES

The Digital Television Network is considering an appeal to the Independent Television Commission over its decision to award the British digital terrestrial television licence to the rival British Sky Broadcasting consortium. As part of its case, DTN may appeal to the Office of Fair Trading and UK telecommunications watchdog, Oftel and will consider a full judicial review of the decision.
-- GERMANY LIKELY TO AGREE ON FUNDING FOR EUROFIGHTER

German finance minister Theo Waigel has provided further indication that the country will back the launch of the Eurofighter aircraft programme, by stating on Tuesday that the project was 'absolutely necessary' for Germany's defence plans. The 40 billion sterling Eurofighter venture, which includes the UK, Italy and Spain, could be jeopardised if Germany delays any further and some 75,000 jobs are on the line. Holding Germany back are proposals to cut the country's defence budget.
-- EDS SEALS PRIVATE FINANCE DEAL ON AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL

UK computer services company Electronic Data Systems is set to be awarded the first private finance initiative contract from the Labour government. The 53 million sterling air traffic control contract will require EDS to install a system at the Oceanic control centre in Prestwick, Scotland which is designed to cut travel times, improve safety and allow for an annual growth in transatlantic traffic of between four and six per cent.
-- BT TO OFFER SHOPPERS FREE CALLS

In an attempt to reduce the flow of customers from it to rivals groups, British Telecommunications has unveiled its latest customer-attracting scheme - TalkTime. J Sainsbury, Barclaycard and Texaco have teamed up with BT for the venture which transfers cash spent with the retailers will count towards free minutes of call time subtracted from BT customers' quarterly bills. Customers will not have to be BT subscribers, as they will be able to donate credits to nominated BT customers.
-- THREAT TO PUT CONTROLS ON BEEF IMPORTS

Britain's agriculture minister Jack Cunningham has warned his EU partners that unless they introduce UK-style safeguards against the spread of 'mad cow' disease he will level import controls on European beef. Speaking to the EU ministers in Luxembourg, Cunningham stressed the need to exclude from the food chain the animal parts which are most at risk of carrying BSE, imposing a July 22 deadline for action to be taken in the EU.

Swiss-based luxury products group Vendome has announced the acquisition of the Vacheron and Constantin watchmaker groups, and the loss of service of French fashion designer Karl Lagerfield. Vendome chairman Joseph Kanoui stated the loss of the Lagerfield brand should have no significant effect on revenues at the company which also released its first-quarter results. Pre-tax profits rose eight per cent to a record SFr509.9m and sales up 12 per cent to SFr3bn. Vendome's best market was in North America.
-- HAMILL A CONTENDER AT WH SMITH

Keith Hamill, WH Smith's finance director, has been tipped as the likely successor to Bill Cockburn, who resigned from his position as chief executive at the company on Monday. Hammill has been with the company for just one year and is well known for his role in defending Forte in its hostile takeover bid battle with the Granada Group. WH Smith chairman Jeremy Hardie has revealed the company is looking at both internal and external candidates.
